summary: Edge session-slip causes route-bounce and partial model pin during staged release
description:
Issue summary: During a staged canary release (10% weight) for redwood-gpt-13b-quant-v2, a subset of customer requests from Skylark Media experienced transient 'route-bounce'—requests initially routed to the edge shard A then retried and served by edge shard B which had a different session cache state. Impact: ~7% of the customer's requests during the window returned mixed model outputs or triggered fallback routing to the default variant, causing increased latency and user-facing quality regressions. Environment: production, us-west region, dedicated tenancy for Skylark Media.

Observed behavior: some long-lived chat sessions were partially pinned to the canary variant on the downstream serving runtime while edge shard state indicated no pin; subsequent requests from the same logical session went to the stable variant or fallback path, leading to mixed outputs and a cascade of retries. Health probes briefly reported elevated request error rates for the canary pool which triggered defensive shedding and expanded fallback routing.

Why this is unique: unlike earlier 'pin split' incidents, this one appears correlated with edge-level session duplication during a background reshard (edge-reshard) that coincided with the staged rollout window. The reshard produced duplicate session tokens (session-slip) with identical session identifiers but different shard-resident affinity metadata, resulting in conflicting pin writes to the control plane and ephemeral route divergence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a staged canary (10% weight) for redwood-gpt-13b-quant-v2 targeting us-west.
2) Simulate a Skylark-like SDK client that performs long-polling chat with occasional retries (idempotency token present).
3) Trigger an edge reshard event (can be simulated in staging by toggling edge-proxy instance group membership).
4) Observe session cache divergence between edge shards and monitor routing decisions / pin writes in the control plane.
5) Reproduce by replaying recorded client traffic through two different edge shard instances to validate partial pin writes and fallback triggers.

comments: Maya Rodriguez (Support): Customer reported 'sometimes the chat answers flip mid-session after retrying' — they provided SDK traces and request ids.
Ethan Cole (SRE): Initial triage indicates edge reshard coincident with the rollout window. Captured edge-proxy logs show same session_id served by two different shards.
Priya Shah (Routing Eng): Hypothesis: session-slip duplicates session cookies between transient shards; control-plane pin write is non-idempotent for this path and can result in partial commits.

Ethan Cole (SRE): Temporary mitigation suggested: increase canary route cookie affinity TTL to prefer single-shard stickiness during rollouts and block automatic reshard operations for custodial tenancies during staged rollouts.
Customer (Skylark Media): Provided repro traffic and agreed to a short coordinated test window in staging on 2026-03-12.
Priya Shah (Routing Eng): Added instrumentation to pin-write flow to log idempotency tokens and shard origin for next 24h. Patch PR created: github.com/redwood/router/pull/2190.
Ethan Cole (SRE): Scheduled a rollback of the reshard job during active canaries as an immediate operational control.
investigation_notes: Edge reshard job was running every 5 minutes; during a reshard the session cache is briefly rebuilt which correlates with the timeframe in logs.
Control-plane accepts pin-writes from any edge shard without cross-shard validation; in this case two different shards wrote conflicting pin metadata within 200ms.
Idempotency token present in SDK was identical but not enforced by the control-plane pin API; duplicate writes were treated as separate operations.

Health-probe reaction amplified the issue: canary pool saw a small error-rate spike which triggered shedding and fallback expansion, causing more traffic to be routed away and increasing mixed-output reports.
action_plan: Short-term (operational): Disable reshard jobs for dedicated tenancies while any staged canary is active. Coordinate with Customer Success to schedule re-rollouts.
Mid-term (engineering): Add origin-shard metadata to pin-write RPC and make pin-write idempotent by (session_id + idempotency_token + shard_origin) dedupe semantics.

Long-term (platform): Introduce an edge-global session coordinator to prevent session-slip during instance membership changes; add a gating policy that pauses resharding during canary windows for pinned sessions.
QA/Testing: Create a synthetic replay test that exercises cross-shard session replay and asserts control-plane pin coherence under reshard events.
resolution: In Progress - operational mitigations applied (reshard jobs disabled during active canaries for affected tenancy). Engineering patch PRs authored and new pin-write instrumentation deployed to staging for validation. Awaiting staged replay test results scheduled 2026-03-12. Postmortem and follow-up tasks to be created if validation confirms fix.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-2190: Implement pin-write idempotency and shard-origin validation
OPS-1121: Add rollout gating to resharder for dedicated tenancies
QA-78: Synthetic cross-shard session replay test and automation
